title: Architecture & Standards: Unified Guidelines (API, Coding, Infra, Serving, Observability, Performance, ADRs)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards across API design, code quality, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, performance SLOs, and the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) process. It is intended as the single-entry reference for product teams, infra, and platform engineers when designing or evolving services that serve inference workloads.

Use this document to: 
- Evaluate new designs against company-wide constraints and expectations.
- Find concrete thresholds, example configs, and owners.
- Learn the ADR workflow for recording decisions that impact operations, cost, and customer-facing behavior.

1) API Standards

Principles:
- Backwards compatibility is primary for public SDK/REST surfaces. Breaking changes require a deprecation plan (90 days for hosted API, see Release Notes).
- Consistency: request/response shapes, metadata headers, and error codes must be uniform across services.
- Observability first: every API route must emit structured tracing, latency, and request-size metrics.

Requirements (minimum):
- HTTP: use RESTful routes with resource-based paths (POST /v1/runs, GET /v1/models/{id}/metadata).
- Versioning: include major version in the path (v1, v2). Support content negotiation via Accept header for beta features.
- Auth: token-based Authorization: Bearer <token>. Private deployments may integrate KMS-backed tokens; consult eng-private-deployments/ onprem-packaging.
- Rate limiting: endpoints must honor x-rw-quota headers and return 429 with Retry-After on quota breach.
- Errors: JSON body with fields {"code": "SOME_CODE", "message": "human readable", "request_id": "<uuid>"}. Map service errors to a canonical list in the API standards catalog.

Headers and telemetry (must be present):
- X-RW-Request-Id: UUID generated at API gateway.
- X-RW-Tenant: tenant id (when applicable).
- Traceparent / tracestate for distributed tracing.

Example request/response snippets and OpenAPI requirements are maintained in eng-developer-experience/api-examples.

2) Coding Standards

Principles:
- Maintainability: small modules, clear abstractions.
- Testability: unit tests for logic, integration tests for persistence and network edges.
- Safety: linting, CI checks, and fuzz tests for public parsers.

Requirements by language (summary):
- Python: follow PEP8 + pyproject.toml settings, type annotations for public interfaces, mypy strict for SDK modules.
- Go: gofmt, vet, and staticcheck before merge. Error wrapping with %w and sentinel errors documented.
- Rust/C++ (runtime): documented unsafe blocks with justification and safety invariants in comments.

CI gating: PRs must pass unit tests, linters, and a smoke integration job that runs model-mock service integration. Size limits: PRs > 500 LOC must include a design summary in PR description.

Code ownership: each repository must have CODEOWNERS configured; critical infra repos require oncall rotation defined in eng-sre/runbooks.

3) Infrastructure Standards

Principles:
- Reproducible: everything deployable via Terraform modules and immutable artifacts.
- Least privilege: cloud IAM policies follow the principle of least privilege and are reviewed quarterly.
- Multi-region readiness: services must be deployable to at least two regions for dedicated/hosted tiers.

Network and security requirements:
- VPCs: use Terraform modules under eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking; default flow logs enabled and sent to central logging.
- KMS: keys for customer data encryption at rest must be customer-specific for Private deployments; Hosted uses company KMS with separation boundaries.
- Secrets: no secrets in repo; use Vault (or cloud-secret-manager) with automatic rotation.

Capacity & autoscaling patterns:
- Inference pools (Dedicated): use horizontal autoscaling based on GPU utilization (target 60-70%) and queue length. Burst capacity must be implemented with a separate worker pool and subject to quota checks.
- CI/CD: every infra change requires a plan output and drift check in pipeline.

4) Model-Serving Standards

Principles:
- Reproducible model artifacts with pinned hashes and provenance metadata.
- Transparent fallbacks: routing policies must declare compatible fallback models and degradation behavior.

Requirements and configs:
- Model packaging: models must include metadata.json with fields: name, version, architecture, quantization_profile, kv_cache_compatible (true/false), and cpu_offload_support.
- Runtime capability matrix: each model must be validated against the serving runtime matrix (latency profile, memory working set, supported sequence lengths). See eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
- KV cache policy: services must declare prefix cache TTLs and invalidation hooks. Default prefix cache TTL = 24h for stable prompts, configurable per-tenant.

Operational behaviors:
- Model rollouts: use canary (5%) -> 25% -> 100% with automated quality checks (see Apply-ML eval-harness). Canary windows: minimum 2 hours and must pass latency, error-rate, and quality thresholds before next step.
- Fallback policy: define primary, fallback-1, fallback-2 in the routing config. Fallbacks must be compatible tokenizers and response-shaped.

5) Observability Standards

Principles:
- Signal over noise: collect high-signal metrics and instrument tracing for latency-critical paths.
- Correlation: logs, traces, and metrics must be linkable by X-RW-Request-Id and trace ids.

Minimum telemetry (per service):
- Metrics: request_count, request_errors (4xx/5xx split), p50/p90/p99 latency (server and end-to-end), tokens_out_per_minute, gpu_utilization, vm_memory_pressure.
- Tracing: span for gateway auth, model routing, runtime evaluate, kv-cache lookup, token-generation loop.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with level, timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, route, error_code.

Alerting & dashboards:
- SLO-based alerts: to be derived from SLOs below. High-severity pager if SLI breach > 1 hour or error rate spike > 5x baseline.
- Dashboard templates: use eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts templates for per-model and per-route dashboards.

6) Performance Standards & SLOs

Global SLO targets (hosted API default):
- Availability: 99.95% monthly for control plane endpoints (management APIs).
- Latency: 95% of generation requests should meet per-model latency profile; default target p95 < 1.2s for short-chat workloads (<=256 tokens) on curated models.
- Error budget: 0.05% monthly error budget for user-facing requests.

Performance testing and benchmarking:
- Bench harness: use eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite with representative traces and token distributions.
- Load testing: every major change to scheduling/kernel selection must run the benchmark suite and submit results to perf dashboards.
- Quantization regressions: any new quantization profile must be run through the regression-triage process and evaluated with the eval-harness prompt set.

7) ADR (Architecture Decision Record) Process

Purpose: capture trade-offs and rationale for decisions that materially affect operations, cost, or developer ergonomics.

When to open an ADR:
1. New architecture component with team-wide impact (e.g., switching orchestration, adopting new kernel library).
2. Breaking API changes or versioning policy shifts.
3. Major infra policy changes (network topology, encryption boundary).

ADRs must include (template):
- Title, date, status (proposed | accepted | superseded | deprecated).
- Context: problem statement and constraints.
- Decision: chosen option and what is being changed.
- Consequences: operational, cost, and developer impacts.
- Rollout Plan: steps, owners, monitoring, rollback criteria.
- Related ADRs and links.

Workflow:
1. Draft ADR in repo under docs/adrs/<short-name>.md and assign reviewers (default reviewers: architecture guild + owning team).
2. Review window: 5 business days. If significant, post to arch-review channel and schedule architecture sync.
3. If accepted, create a Confluence summary page and tag with label "adrs". Update related runbooks and SLOs.

Example ADR (summary):
- Title: "Use GPU-aware scheduling in the runtime"
- Decision: adopt gang-scheduling + CUDA IPC fast-path for multi-model batching.
- Consequences: improve throughput by ~20% on long-sequence workloads; increases scheduler complexity and requires node-level isolation changes.

8) Governance, Review Cadence, and Owners

- Standards owner: Architecture Guild (rotating leads with record in eng-platform/roadmap). Primary contact: Diego Ramirez.
- Review cadence: annual review for API and infra standards, quarterly for observability/performance thresholds.
- Exceptions: documented under security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions with an expiration date and mitigation plan.

Appendix A: Example Config Snippets

Model metadata (models/<name>/metadata.json) example:
{
  "name": "refined-chat-7b",
  "version": "2026-02-01",
  "architecture": "transformer-gpt",
  "quantization_profile": "q4_0",
  "kv_cache_compatible": "true",
  "sequence_length_max": "8192"
}

Routing policy example (YAML):
- name: customer-default-route
  primary: refined-chat-7b
  fallbacks: ["refined-chat-7b-quantized", "refined-chat-6b"]
  canary: 0.05

SLO reporting example (text):
- SLI: p95 latency (short-chat)
- SLO: p95 < 1.2s monthly
- Alert: Pager if p95 > 1.6s sustained for 15m

References and links:
- eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture (runtime architecture and kernel selection)
- eng-developer-experience/api-examples (OpenAPI and SDK guidelines)
- eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets (SLO definition and incident playbooks)
- applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness (quality checks for rollouts)

Revision history:
- 2024-10-15: initial draft (Aisha Patel).
- 2025-06-09: added model metadata and rollout policy details (Maya Chen).
- 2026-02-20: harmonized SLO targets and expanded ADR workflow (Diego Ramirez).

If you are proposing a change to these standards, open an ADR and ping the Architecture Guild.
